stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

The committee has decided to move its meeting to Friday.
hints: "Committee" names a group of people. In this sentence, is the group acting together, as one?
The committee made one decision together. A group that acts as one unit is treated as singular, like "it".
Check each part: does the verb fit a singular subject? Does the pronoun fit a singular subject? Is the small linking word right? If all three parts pass, the sentence has no error.

solution.methodName: Find the true subject, then match the verb

steps.action: Find the subject: "The committee". It is a collective noun.
steps.why: A collective noun is a word for a group, such as committee, team, family or staff.

steps.action: Decide if the group acts as one. It does: the committee made one decision together. So treat "committee" as singular.
steps.why: In the exam, a group acting as one unit takes a singular verb, as if you said "it".

steps.action: Check "has decided": a singular verb for a singular subject. Correct.
Check "to move its meeting": "its" is singular and matches "committee". Correct.
Check "to Friday": you move a meeting to a new day. Correct.
All three parts are correct, so the answer is "No error".

trapNotes.has decided: A committee has many members, so "have decided" may feel right. But here the committee acts as one group, so the singular "has" is correct.
trapNotes.to move its meeting: Some think "its" should be "their" because a committee has many people. Since the group acts as one, "its" is correct, and it matches "has".
trapNotes.to Friday: This part is correct. You move a meeting to a new day. "To Friday" tells where the meeting goes on the calendar.
